Opposite Party :- State of U.P. and Another Counsel for Applicant :- Gaurav Kakkar,Ambuj Pandey Counsel for Opposite Party :- Govt. Advocate Hon'ble Sanjay Kumar Singh,J.
Heard learned counsel for the applicants, learned Additional Government Advocate for the State/opposite party no.1 and Mr. C.P. Upadhyay, learned counsel for opposite party no. 2.

This application under Section 482 Cr.P.C. has been filed by the applicants to quash the charge-sheet dated 01.03.2012 arising out of Case Crime No. 213 of 2011 and proceedings of Case No. 313 of 2012, under Section 498A IPC and Section 3/4 Dowry Prohibition Act, Police Station Badalpur, District Gautam Budh Nagar pending in the court of Judicial Magistrate, Gautam Budh Nagar.

sentences.text: It is an old case of the year 2012.
Brief facts of the case which are required to be stated are that applicant no. 1 is son-in-law of opposite party no. 2.
Applicant nos. 2, 3, 4, 5, 6 and 7 are father, uncle, mother, sister-in-law (bhabhi) and brothers of applicant no. 1, respectively.

Opposite party no. 2 lodged a first information report on 23.10.2011 under Section 498A IPC and Section 3/4 Dowry Prohibition Act against the applicants alleging inter alia that marriage of his daughter Sanju Rani was solemnized on 09.12.2008 with applicant no. 1 as per the Hindu Customs and Rites and he had spent a sum of Rs.
12.50 lacs approximately but after 15 days of marriage, the accused persons started harassing his daughter putting further demand of Rs. 5 lacs and she faced all sorts of abuses, physical and mental torture.
She tried to convince them but they did not listen to her.
When all efforts failed, his daughter called his younger son on 16.06.2010 to her matrimonial home, who brought her to her parental home.
Then she narrated everything.

He made efforts to settle the matter and in this case,
4-5 meetings were also held but the accused persons were bent upon their demand of Rs. 5 lacs, as such, efforts to settle the matter failed on 10.09.2011.

After culmination of investigation,
charge-sheet was submitted on 01.03.2012 against the applicants, on which, Magistrate concerned took cognizance on 03.03.2012.
The aforesaid charge-sheet is the subject matter of challenge in the present case.
It is submitted by learned counsel for the applicants that on 05.12.2012, when this matter was heard at initial stage, the relief as sought for by applicant no. 1 was refused.
So far as applicant nos. 2 to 7 are concerned, interim order in their favour was passed directing that till the next date of listing,
further

proceeding against applicant nos. 2 to 7, namely, Santosh Sharma, Surendra Sharma, Smt.
Raj Kumari, Smt. Rekha Sharma, Mahesh Sharma and Manish Kumar
shall remain stayed.

During pendency of this application, applicant nos. 2 and 4, namely, Santosh Sharma and Smt. Raj Kumari,
who are father and mother of applicant no. 1 has died, and at present, case of only applicant nos. 3,
5, 6 and 7 is pending for consideration on merits.

Main substratum of argument of learned counsel for the applicants is that neither there is specific allegation against applicant nos. 3, 5, 6 and 7 in the first information report nor found during investigation.
Applicant nos. 3, 5, 6 and 7 have been implicated in this case because they are relatives of applicant no. 1.

It is further submitted that general allegations have been levelled against applicant nos. 3, 5, 6 and 7 without attributing any specific role and mentioning even single incident against them as to how they were involved in the alleged incident.

Lastly, learned counsel for the applicants relying on the judgments of the Apex Court in the cases of Geeta Mehrotra and another Vs. State of U.P. and another, (2012) 10 SCC 741 and Kahkashan Kausar @ Sonam and others Vs.
State of Bihar and others, (2022) 6 SCC 599 submits that impugned charge-sheet dated 01.03.2012 as well as further criminal proceedings pursuant thereto against the applicant nos. 3, 5, 6 and 7 is liable to be quashed.

Per contra, learned Additional Government Advocate for the State as well as learned counsel for opposite party no. 2 opposed the relief as sought for by applicant nos. 3, 5, 6 and 7 reiterating the prosecution case as mentioned in the first information report and they have also submitted that in the harassment and torture of daughter of opposite party no. 2, all the accused persons were Satish Sharma And Others vs State Of U.P. And Another on 21 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/88976691/
2 involved, therefore, they are equally liable.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
It is also submitted that daughter of opposite party no. 2 has also filed a case under Section 125 Cr.P.C. against applicant no. 1, in which order for giving maintenance to her has been passed by Family Court but the same is not being paid by applicant no.
1.

Lastly, it is submitted that offence under Section 498A IPC and Section 3/4 Dowry Prohibition Act is also made out against applicant nos. 3, 5, 6 and 7, therefore, instant application is liable to be dismissed.

Having heard submission of learned counsel for the parties and examined the record, I find that omnibus allegations have been levelled against all the accused persons without attributing specific role to applicant nos. 3, 5, 6 and 7.

Record indicates that during investigation, matter was referred to mediation vide order dated 17.11.2021 in Criminal Misc. Writ Petition No. 21438 of 2011 but it appears that mediation could not succeed.

entities.text: Criminal Misc. Writ Petition No. 21438 of 2011
entities.label: CASE_NUMBER

sentences.text: I also find that the relief so far as applicant no. 1, who is husband of Smt. Sanju Rani (daughter of opposite party no. 2), is concerned, the same has already been refused by this Court as noted above and he is facing trial.

In the light of aforesaid judgments of the Apex Court in the case Geeta Mehrotra (supra) and Kahkashan (supra), case of applicant nos.
3, 5, 6 and 7 is distinguishable from the case of applicant no. 1 and the charge-sheet against them is liable to be quashed as criminal prosecution against them on the general allegation is abuse of process of the Court.

Hence, in order to secure the ends of justice, charge-sheet dated 01.03.2012 so far as it relates to applicant nos. 3, 5, 6 and 7 as well as criminal proceedings of the above case pursuant thereto is hereby quashed.
This application under Section 482 Cr.P.C. in respect of applicant nos. 2 and 4, namely, Santosh Sharma and Smt. Raj Kumari is abated as they have died during pendency of this application.
So far as applicant nos. 3, 5, 6 and 7, namely, Surendra Sharma, Smt. Rekha Sharma, Mahesh Sharma and Manish Kumar are concerned, the application stands allowed.
